# Bound to be Complete: Efficient Verification for SQL Equivalence via U-Expressions

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#sqlution)

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.28516v1) · arXiv:2611.28516v1, 21 November 2026, 14 pages.

**Reading coverage:** Read the entire posted article, Sections 1–11, Algorithm 1, theorems, worked examples, tables and figure captions. Visually checked Tables 3–4 and Figure 4 on PDF pages 10–11. The separate proof supplement is an outstanding reading gap.

## Research question

Executing two plausible SQL programs on the current data can hide differences that would appear on another database satisfying the same constraints.

## Method

The verifier translates SQL into functions that count result-tuple multiplicities. It expands sums over a bounded set of distinct symbolic input tuples and asks Z3 for a database that separates the queries. Deterministic ordering adds a check for a pair of rows in different relative orders. Integrity constraints restrict the search.

## Evaluation

The Spider workload pairs DAIL-SQL predictions with references. The authors set aside 37 of 1,034 pairs because of ambiguous SQL ordering and label the remaining 997 using verifiers and manual inspection when necessary. Two further workloads use 127 mutated Spark pairs and Cubes tasks with 100 queries each. Baselines include Polygon and VeriEQL.

## What the results support

At bound four SQLution found 269 of the 271 known non-equivalent Spider pairs. The authors found the remaining two at bound ten. On mutually supported non-equivalent Spider cases Table 4 gives median verification times of 8.0 ms for SQLution and 47.4 ms for Polygon. These times measure how long it takes to distinguish queries, not the queries’ execution speed.

## Limits and qualifications

The guarantee assumes supported SQL, satisfiable integrity constraints for the witness and a solver that can decide the formula. An exhausted search within one bound cannot settle global equivalence. Window functions, recursive CTEs and nondeterministic tie ordering are outside the described support. The separate proofs and executable release were not verified.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

A counterexample can distinguish two candidate interpretations that happen to agree on current data. Deciding which interpretation answers the question requires separate evidence. The paper evaluates the query-pair check, without evaluating clarification or abstention.
